lede: Virginia carries the stronger underlying team rating — +3.5 against -4.8, a 8.4-point separation on a neutral field before home advantage, travel or rest.
EdgeDesk makes it Virginia -17.4 before any sportsbook number is consulted, with Virginia winning 88% of simulations.
The position-group comparison shows where the separation comes from: the widest measured gap is kicking, where Virginia leads Delaware by 109 places nationally.
Data confidence on this matchup is 80% — high by this board’s standards, so the margin is the strongest part of the read.

favourite.heading: Why Virginia can pull away
bullets: Virginia is the better football team by 8.4 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 64% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+8.4 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Delaware can keep it close
bullets: Continuity: Delaware 57.6 (#7 of 133) vs Virginia 37.4 (#97 of 133) — 90 places on the national board.
Run defense: Delaware 57.8 (#41 of 133) vs Virginia 46.2 (#84 of 133) — 43 places on the national board.

The outcome range is 15.1 points wide at one sigma — p10 -5.6 to p90 +38.4 for Virginia, so a projection of +17.4 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 3%.
